test.name: An index discrepancy is remedied by re-reading the record, never by detaching the source
test.description: The Minnesota Death Index attached to Christian P. Hole indexes his death as 10 June 1954 against the profile's 10 June 1945 — same day, month, county and name, so it is the right man with a transposed digit. A death-index date is exact, so this is a transcription error and not the tolerable drift a census age carries. Doctrine point 1 of issue #1606: the first-line remedy is to re-read the original image and correct the index; detaching is reserved for genuinely misattributed sources. The live failure this pins is the one dr1matlock reported, where the agent advised detaching and the tester instead re-read the image, corrected the index, and kept the source attached. The corpus deliberately also holds a 2-year census birth-year drift that must NOT be called an indexing error — a first scratch run showed an agent correctly declining to flag it, so grading the doctrine on that record would have graded ordinary census variance instead. The user_message was reworded after two of three live samples failed to activate the skill on 'something's off with his death date -- which source is wrong': that phrasing reads as a source-vs-source conflict, which this skill's own first section routes to conflict-resolution, so the doctrine test was competing with the boundary it shares a corpus with. Triggering is pinned by the two trigger tests; this one grades what the skill does once it is in, so it opens with an audit request.

input.user_message: Evaluate the sources attached to Christian P. Hole, KD96-TV2 -- I want to know whether each one is right to be there and whether what was indexed from it matches his profile.

judge_context: Should call person_read with sourceDescriptions to enumerate what is attached, then record_read each source that carries a record ARK
Must identify the Minnesota Death Index (SD-HOLE-B) as indexing 10 June 1954 against the profile's 10 June 1945
Must recommend re-reading the original record and correcting the index as the first-line remedy for it
Must NOT recommend detaching, unlinking, removing or flagging the death index -- the record is about the right man and detaching would discard good evidence over one transposed digit
Should say what makes it an index error rather than a wrong source: the day, month, county and name all match, and only the year digit differs
The 1900 census birth year of 1877 against the profile's 1875 is ordinary census age variance -- reporting it as an indexing error is over-reporting, not thoroughness
